title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with activity as satellite demand surges and regulatory changes reshape the landscape. Meanwhile, competition with China and emerging defense technologies continue to dominate discussions.

themes.title: Satellite Demand on the Rise
themes.body: Airbus is capitalizing on the growing appetite for satellite systems, positioning itself well in a competitive market. This trend reflects a broader shift as nations and companies prioritize space capabilities.

themes.title: Regulatory Changes Ahead
themes.body: The FCC's sweeping reforms and new C-band auction are set to reshape the satellite licensing landscape, potentially easing congestion for operators. These changes could pave the way for more efficient deployment of satellite services.

themes.title: Defense Tech Collaboration
themes.body: Anduril and L3Harris's partnership on a tactical SDA constellation bid highlights the increasing integration of commercial tech in defense strategies. This trend signals a shift towards more agile and responsive military capabilities.

themes.title: China's Orbital Maneuvers
themes.body: China's Shijian-31 satellite is making waves with its unique GEO orbit, raising eyebrows among international observers. Such advancements underscore the strategic competition in space and the need for vigilance.
